record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X, μ) on itself unbalanced in the sense of Allison and Panagiotopoulos, and if so does this remain true after restricting to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Actually, their work also provides a dynamical analogue of turbulence called unbalancedness which rules out Borel reduction to equivalence relations coming from actions of Polish groups admitting a compatible biinvariant metric, so a positive answer to the following question implies a negative answer to Question 4.3.
Question 4.4. Is the conjugacy action of Aut(X, µ) on itself unbalanced? If yes, is it still if we restrict to ergodic transformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard atomless probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $(X,\mu)$ (modulo null sets), equipped with the weak topology. The group $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ acts on itself by conjugation: $g\cdot T = gTg^{-1}$.

Recall the following notion (due to Allison and Panagiotopoulos): a continuous action of a Polish group $G$ on a Polish space $Y$ is called \emph{unbalanced} if there is no Borel-definable way to assign, in a $G$-invariant manner, points of a Polish space carrying a Polish group action with a compatible bi-invariant metric; more precisely, the orbit equivalence relation $E^Y_G$ is not Borel reducible to any orbit equivalence relation induced by a continuous action of a Polish group admitting a compatible two-sided invariant metric. (Equivalently, the action exhibits a generic "unbalanced" dynamical obstruction in the sense of the games-orbits-play framework.)

Questions:
(a) Is the conjugation action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ on itself unbalanced?
(b) If yes, does this remain true when the action is restricted to the set of ergodic measure-preserving transformations (which is a $G_\delta$ invariant subset of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$)?
artifact.category_tag: descriptive set theory and ergodic actions
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 arXiv preprint titled "Unbalancedness of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations" (arXiv:2510.04989) proves that the isomorphism relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is unbalanced, i.e., it is not Borel reducible to any orbit equivalence relation arising from a Polish group action with a compatible bi-invariant metric. This answers both parts of the question affirmatively, including the restriction to ergodic transformations.

status_evidence.title: Unbalancedness of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations
status_evidence.snippet: The isomorphism of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the relation induced by the conjugacy action of the full group of an ergodic measure-preserving transformation on itself.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes unbalancedness of the conjugation action restricted to ergodic transformations, affirmatively answering the question.
